title: Open-restriction comparison data for sheaf dg scalar adjunctions
statement: For the site, coefficient sheaf and dg notions of [def-sfb-ringed-site-dg-modules], restriction to an object $U$ is restriction of the actual coefficient complexes by the sheaf-module functor to the slice site $C/U$. An open restriction of $A$ to $A_U$ consists of an isomorphism of the underlying restricted algebra complexes preserving multiplication sectionwise, a module restriction functor with a natural underlying-complex comparison preserving actions sectionwise, and its localization with the natural comparison to the module restriction. (The unit is then preserved since an invertible multiplicative map preserves units.) For a scalar model of $\varphi:A\to B$, compatible open data consist of such restrictions for both algebras, a map $\varphi_U:A_U\to B_U$ intertwining $\varphi$, standard derived structures and a scalar model on the slice, a module-level isomorphism between restricting along $\varphi$ and then to $U$ and restricting to $U$ and then along $\varphi_U$ whose underlying map is the identity of the restricted complexes (through the two underlying comparisons), and natural isomorphisms identifying restricted derived restriction and extension with the corresponding slice functors; the restriction comparison is, at every localized module, the transport of that module-level isomorphism through the localization factorizations. Their adjunction units and action counits commute with these comparison isomorphisms: after the restriction comparison and then the extension comparison, the global unit becomes the slice unit; the analogous counit square commutes. On the open site of a space, $C/U$ is canonically the open site of the subspace $U$. These are definitions of comparison data; existence is not part of this definition.
